source.title: P$^2$ Law: Scaling Law for Post-Training After Model Pruning
source.authors: Xiaodong Chen; Yuxuan Hu; Xiao-Kang Zhang; Yanling Wang; Cui-Ping Li; Hong Chen; Jing Zhang

record.file_problem: none; the full paper, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study extends scaling-law analysis to post-training pruned language models and reports loss curves, fits, and generalization results in that setting.
record.gate_note: The paper tests a scaling law for validation loss during post-training after pruning, not the original held-out pretraining-loss law. It reports its own loss-curve and fit/generalization results. Results cited from Kaplan et al., Hoffmann et al., and other prior work are not recorded as findings. Downstream-task results and comparisons of model architecture shape are not reported.
record.test_reason: The study fits a Chinchilla-form power law (with pre-pruning loss and pruning-rate terms) to validation loss during continual post-training of pruned Llama-3 and Qwen-2.5 models. It reports fit quality and held-out generalization. This bears on V5, since the same form is tested in a new training regime. It bears weakly on V2 through small-to-larger-model prediction. The scale gap is only about 2–5x, not orders of magnitude.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely right. The authors also claim the law generalizes to larger model sizes: despite poor R² and Huber loss, low ASD shows it predicts the optimal compute point. They present this as confirmed feasibility rather than as a weakness.
record.recipe_differences: This is a scaling-law study of validation loss during post-training after pruning, with pruning rate and pre-pruning loss included in its proposed formulation; it is not the original pretraining scaling-law setup.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes depend on pruning method and model: width pruning on Llama-3.1-8B is anomalous. The study also reports differences among candidate parameterizations and weaker absolute-fit results when transferring from smaller to larger models.

fits_no_version.finding: Relative post-training loss scales as a power of inverse pruning rate; the fit generalizes from lower to higher pruning rates (R² about 0.97).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Post-pruning recovery loss follows a power law in pruning rate.

fits_no_version.finding: Smaller pruned models recover loss faster per post-training token.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Post-training loss slope after pruning decreases with pre-pruning model size.

fits_no_version.finding: Selection among the authors' own law forms: Chinchilla-form candidates (L1) fit better than Kaplan-form candidates (L4, L5) and than L2/L3.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Choice of functional form changes fit quality for post-pruning loss laws.

record.problems: The tested models are restricted to fewer than 8B parameters; the authors state that GPU-resource limits prevented larger-scale experiments. Model-size generalization has poor R² and Huber loss despite low ASD. No uncertainty estimates are reported. Table 6 conflicts with prose about whether all fitted L1 parameterizations satisfy the stated conditions.
record.rows_left_out: Figures show many individual loss curves and Tables 2–3 report multiple parameterization/generalization metrics by model series and pruning method. These are not separately enumerated here; rows prioritize the stated aggregate trends, the explicit anomalous case, and the generalization outcomes. The study's authors state that additional curves exhibit similar trends.

untested.parts: Pretraining loss vs parameters, tokens or compute is not measured.
Extrapolation over orders of magnitude; the only cross-size test spans about 2–5x within 0.5B–8B models.
No compute-optimal allocation of parameters vs tokens.
No shape variation at fixed parameter count.
Other modalities, repeated data, and fine-tuning or transfer without pruning.
Published pretraining laws' exponent dependence on setup is not studied. Only the authors' own candidate forms are compared.

missing.what: Model-size generalization under depth pruning: Llama R² -0.5441, Qwen R² -0.8786, with low ASD.
Kaplan-form (L4, L5) vs Chinchilla-form (L1) fits; Kaplan forms fit worse, e.g. Qwen depth L4 R² 0.7730.
Fitted constants vary widely across series and pruning methods, including negative α (e.g. -1.57, -3.73, -21.89).

record.verdict_notes: The setting is continual post-training on SlimPajama, up to 1B tokens, with models of 8B parameters or fewer and no uncertainty estimates. Width-pruned Llama-3.1-8B is excluded from the generalization experiments. The record's claimed Table 6 inconsistency does not exist.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test held-out pretraining loss as a power law in parameters, tokens, or compute.
It tests validation within a post-training run and transfer across model sizes in pruned models, not predictions of ordinary pretraining runs orders of magnitude larger.
It does not jointly optimize parameter count and token count at a fixed compute budget or estimate their growth exponents.
It does not vary depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count to measure their effect on loss.
The tested regime is post-training after pruning of text language models. Other modalities, repeated-data regimes, fine-tuning without pruning, and transfer settings are not tested.

The study compares candidate fit parameterizations and reports a pruning/model-specific anomaly, but does not systematically vary parameter counting, schedules, datasets, or fitting methods to estimate their effects on exponents or compute-optimal splits.

rows.subject: Llama-3 and Qwen-2.5 series (aggregate)
rows.size_stated: 0.5B–8B; Llama-3.1-8B is the largest tested model
rows.operation_detail: Measured validation loss as post-training tokens increased for models pruned by depth, width, or 2:4 semi-structured pruning.

conditions.value: depth, width, and 2:4 semi-structured; multiple rates
up to 0.5B or 1B, depending on model

rows.value: The paper states that post-training loss decreases as the number of post-training tokens increases.
rows.note: Aggregate textual statement about the tested post-training curves; this is not a result on unpruned pretraining loss.
rows.check: Monotonic loss decrease with tokens is the authors' Condition 1. It cannot by itself show a power-law form; the fit evidence is in r4/r5/r8.

rows.subject: Llama-3 and Qwen-2.5 series (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Compared loss-curve slopes across model sizes at similar pruning rates.
rows.measure: Rate of validation-loss decrease with post-training tokens
rows.value: The paper reports that smaller models' loss curves decrease faster than larger models' curves.
rows.note: The paper describes the trend across pruning methods; it does not provide a fitted power exponent for this size comparison.
rows.check: Qualitative trend (smaller models' loss falls faster) used to build the law's Condition 2. It does not measure any version's power-law form.

rows.subject: Llama-3.1-8B
rows.operation_detail: Compared normalized relative post-training loss across pruning rates.
rows.measure: Normalized relative post-training loss versus post-training tokens
rows.value: The normalized curves at the three pruning rates nearly overlap; the paper says relative loss and pruning rate have a power-law relationship.
rows.note: This is a relationship with pruning rate in a post-pruning regime, not a test of the original parameters/tokens/compute law.
rows.check: Power law in pruning rate is a new variable, not parameters, tokens or compute. Belongs in fits_no_version.

rows.subject: Llama-3 series (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Fitted three candidate P2 Law parameterizations and compared their fit metrics.
rows.measure: Fit quality (R², Huber loss, and ASD)
rows.value: L1 significantly outperforms L2 and L3 on the reported fit metrics.
rows.note: The paper reports the comparison across the Llama-3 series as an aggregate; individual metric values for each pruning-method group are not repeated in this row.
rows.check: This is the study's own parameterization selection (L1 vs L2/L3). Its absolute L1 fit bears on V5: Llama depth R² 0.9717 and 2:4 R² 0.8126, but width R² -1.2985 (all forms negative). The value 'L1 significantly outperforms' hides the negative width R².

rows.subject: Qwen-2.5 series (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Fitted three candidate P2 Law parameterizations and compared their fit metrics.
rows.measure: Fit quality (R², Huber loss, and ASD)
rows.value: L1 significantly outperforms L2 and L3 on the reported fit metrics.
rows.note: The paper reports the comparison across the Qwen-2.5 series as an aggregate.
rows.check: Selection comparison. L1 absolute fit for Qwen is high: depth R² 0.9781, width 0.9891, 2:4 0.9995. The record lists only depth pruning as the condition, but Table 2 covers all three methods.

rows.subject: Llama-3 series (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Fitted candidate parameterizations and checked whether they met the paper's stated conditions for the law.
rows.value: All fitted L1 parameterizations satisfy the three stated conditions; L2 and some fitted L3 parameterizations fail Condition 2. Table 6 also marks L1 as failing Condition 2 for Llama-3 series width pruning.
rows.note: The accompanying prose says all fitted L1 satisfy the conditions, while Table 6 marks Llama-3 series width-pruning L1 with a cross; the text is internally inconsistent on this entry.
rows.check: Constraint compliance of the authors' own candidate forms; it is method selection, not a finding on any version. The record misreads Table 6: Llama width L1 is marked ✓ (L2 and L3 ×), so prose and table agree and there is no inconsistency.

rows.subject: Llama-3.1-8B
rows.operation_detail: Compared loss curves and the applicability of the fitted P2 Law under width pruning.

conditions.value: depth pruning at similar pruning rates

rows.measure: Post-training validation-loss curves and law fit
rows.baseline: Depth-pruned Llama-3.1-8B at similar pruning rates
rows.value: The paper reports anomalous performance: depth pruning outperforms width pruning, contrary to its other cases, and says the law is unsuitable for this special scenario.
rows.note: The authors suggest densely distributed channel-importance scores may explain the width-pruning anomaly.
rows.check: Bears on V5 only. The width-pruned Llama-3.1-8B case is where the law is 'unsuitable'; no V7 link, since it concerns a pruning anomaly, not fitting choices for published laws.

rows.subject: Llama-3 and Qwen-2.5 series (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Fit the P2 Law using the first 80% of checkpoints from each training process and validated on the remaining 20%.

conditions.value: first 80% of checkpoints for fitting; remaining 20% for validation

rows.value: The paper reports that the predicted curves accurately match the validation checkpoints and that the law generalizes to larger dataset sizes.
rows.note: This is a within-run checkpoint holdout in post-training, not an extrapolation across orders of magnitude in ordinary pretraining.
rows.check: Holdout is the last 20% of checkpoints within a run, about a 25% token extension, not orders-of-magnitude extrapolation; drop V2. Table 3 R²: 0.9725/0.9780 depth, 0.9270/0.9896 width, 0.8244/0.9940 2:4.

rows.subject: Qwen-2.5 series (fit on smaller models; tested on Qwen-2.5-3B)
rows.operation_detail: Fit the P2 Law using checkpoints from smaller models and predicted loss curves for the larger model.
rows.measure: Predicted versus actual loss curve, including R², Huber loss, and ASD
rows.value: The paper reports poor R² and Huber loss on the larger unseen model, but low ASD and similar downward slope after training stabilizes; it says the slope may still predict the optimal computation-cost point.
rows.note: Cross-model prediction does not closely match absolute loss values, though the authors report better slope agreement.
rows.check: Wrong condition and subject. The poor R² is for depth pruning: Llama (fit on 1B/3B, predict 8B) R² -0.5441, Qwen R² -0.8786. The cited Qwen width case has R² 0.8627. Drop V7. Low ASD (slope match) is reported throughout.

source_check.correct: For Qwen-2.5 width pruning, fitting on 0.5B and 1.5B and predicting 3B gives R² 0.8627, Huber loss 0.000137, and ASD 0.001772. Negative model-size-generalization R² values belong to depth pruning: Llama −0.5441 and Qwen −0.8786. The stated Qwen subject and width-pruning condition are correct. State: cannot_determine for V2's orders-of-magnitude extrapolation; partial is defensible for V5.
source_check.problem: The value conflates the authors' general description of poor extrapolation with the specific Qwen width result; the experiment does not establish V2's required scale separation.

rows.subject: Qwen-2.5 series (aggregate)
rows.stage_stated: post-training after depth or width pruning
rows.operation_detail: Fit using lower pruning rates and validated using higher pruning rates.

conditions.value: higher rates; width-pruning example uses 0.15 and 0.25 for fitting and 0.35 for validation

rows.value: The paper reports that actual curves closely align with predicted curves and that the law generalizes to higher pruning rates.
rows.note: The paper excludes 2:4 semi-structured pruning from pruning-rate generalization because that method has no pruning-rate variable.
rows.check: Generalization across pruning rate (R² about 0.966–0.971) concerns the study's new variable, not a version's parameters, tokens or compute. Belongs in fits_no_version.

relationships.condition: Post-training after depth or 2:4 pruning, and Qwen-2.5 width pruning
relationships.reason: Chinchilla-form L1 fits post-training loss with R² 0.81–0.9995 (r4, r5) and predicts held-out later checkpoints with R² 0.82–0.99 (r8).
relationships.display_finding: The Chinchilla-form fit achieved R²=0.81–0.9995 for post-training loss and R²=0.82–0.99 when predicting held-out later checkpoints.

source_check.reason: Table 2 gives L1 R² 0.9717 and 0.9781 for depth pruning, 0.8126 and 0.9995 for 2:4 pruning, and 0.9891 for Qwen width pruning. Table 3 supports later-checkpoint generalization in these settings.

relationships.condition: Llama-3 series under width pruning (driven by Llama-3.1-8B)
relationships.reason: All forms give negative R² for Llama width (L1 -1.2985), and the authors call the law unsuitable for width-pruned 8B (r4, r7).
relationships.display_finding: All tested forms had negative R² for Llama width pruning, including −1.2985 for L1, and were deemed unsuitable for width-pruned 8B.

source_check.condition: Llama-3 series under width pruning (driven by Llama-3.1-8B)
source_check.reason: Table 2 reports negative aggregate R² for every tested parameterization under Llama width pruning, including L1 −1.2985. Section 4.2 identifies Llama-3.1-8B as the exception where the law is unsuitable, qualifying its applicability across the series.

relationships.condition: Fitting on smaller pruned models and predicting a 2–5x larger one, depth pruning
relationships.reason: Absolute prediction fails (R² -0.5441 Llama, -0.8786 Qwen) though slope (ASD) is matched; the Qwen width case is moderate (R² 0.8627) (r9).
relationships.display_finding: Depth-pruning predictions matched slopes but yielded R² of −0.5441 for Llama and −0.8786 for Qwen, while Qwen width pruning achieved 0.8627.

relation.reason: Its own fitting and held-out generalization experiments directly assess scaling-law behavior after pruning.

tranche.reason: The study tests an adapted power-law loss formulation in a new training regime: continual post-training after pruning.

source_check.notes: The supplied text is arXiv v3 dated 26 May 2025. The authors interpret low ASD as supporting prediction of a useful computation point despite absolute-loss errors; slope agreement does not establish accurate absolute-loss prediction.

statements.correction: Table 3 model-size generalization: depth-pruned Llama R² −0.5441; depth-pruned Qwen R² −0.8786; width-pruned Qwen R² 0.8627. Section 4.3.2 reports low ASD despite absolute-loss discrepancies. Qwen fitting models: 0.5B and 1.5B; prediction model: 3B. Figure 23a predicts depth-pruned Llama-3.1-8B. Orders-of-magnitude extrapolation: untested.
statements.problem: The pruning fit statistics and slope interpretation are correct, but these modest model-size extrapolations do not test V2's orders-of-magnitude prediction requirement.
